summary: Tokeen Seaplane Base (TKI) is a small public-use seaplane facility serving the remote community of Tokeen on the western coast of Prince of Wales Island in Southeast Alaska. The base provides essential floatplane access for residents and visitors in an area surrounded by the dense temperate rainforest and sheltered waterways of the Alexander Archipelago. It functions primarily as a utility gateway supporting local transportation, fishing, and outdoor recreation in this sparsely populated region.
faqs:
Q: What type of aircraft uses Tokeen Seaplane Base?
A: The facility exclusively serves floatplanes and other seaplane-equipped aircraft, as it is a water-based landing area without runways.

Q: Are there scheduled commercial flights to TKI?
A: Scheduled service is limited; flights are typically operated on an on-demand or charter basis by regional carriers serving Southeast Alaska communities.

Q: What facilities are available at the airport?
A: As a small seaplane base, TKI offers minimal infrastructure, generally limited to a dock or float ramp area; passengers should expect basic services only.

Q: What is the best season to visit?
A: Summer months (May through September) offer the most reliable weather conditions for seaplane operations and access to surrounding wilderness activities.
transport_tips: Access to Tokeen Seaplane Base is primarily by air, as the community has limited road connections on Prince of Wales Island. Travelers typically arrange charter or scheduled floatplane service from larger hubs such as Ketchikan or other Southeast Alaska communities. There is no public transit or rideshare service at the base, so coordinating ground transport in advance is essential.
local_tip: Tides significantly affect floatplane operations here, so always confirm your departure time with the operator based on current tidal conditions in the surrounding sheltered waters.
